answer: A harbor economy can require each agent to lock a scarce, non-transferable membership bond before it earns reputation or receives work. The registry verifies one bond per independently controlled identity, while slashing bonds for duplicate enrollment or provable collusion. This does not make sybils impossible: an attacker can still create identities, but must tie up capital in every one and risks losing it. Basalt and copper might be traded goods; neither substitutes for the bond.
